content: The test image shows a corn ear husked open, revealing dark/black shriveled material replacing the kernels — strongly suggestive of a smut disease. Let me view reference images for the top candidates.
Head_smut reference (bottom-right panel) closely matches the test image. Let me check a few more for confirmation.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Dried corn ear husked open — entire kernel contents completely replaced by dark black, crumbly/powdery spore masses. No individual kernels visible. Dry husk enclosing a cavity full of dark teliospores.

- **Head_smut** (reference, bottom-right panel): Exact match — dried husked ear with dark spore masses replacing all kernel tissue inside. This is the classic presentation of *Sphacelotheca reiliana* destroying the entire ear.

- **Common_smut**: Shows large irregular galls/tumors with greenish-white outer membrane on individual plant parts — very different.

- **All ear rots** (Aspergillus, Diplodia, Gibberella, Trichoderma, Fusarium): Show intact kernels with fungal growth overtop — fundamentally different structure.

The complete conversion of ear contents into a mass of dark teliospores enclosed within dry husks is the defining feature of Head_smut.
